_meta.purpose: IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md W1 — the committed camera rig. Stations are chosen from the data by stated rules so a finished render can be checked against its caption, instead of being picked by eye at render time.
_meta.seed_note: no stochastic step in this script; selection is argmax over stored values and is fully reproducible
_meta.reads_only: this script writes only houdini/cameras.json. Nothing under data/ and nothing in hl_ingest.py is touched.
_meta.units: metres throughout, world frame: +x east, +y up, +z north — the frame envelope.json, highline_footprints.json and Houdini all already share. No swizzle, no rescale.
_meta.no_exaggeration: THE_ANSWERING_LINE.md: no vertical exaggeration anywhere. The camera constants position the viewer; none of them scale geometry. The canopy is small because the towers are the problem — if it reads slight, that is the finding rendering itself correctly.

selection_rules.B_open_contrast: max svf_deck subject to svf_deck >= 0.75 AND river_view

_meta.number_rule: Each station carries the numbers that image is allowed to print, each with its source path. A figure absent from a station's `numbers` block is not board-ready for that plate. Recapture is explicitly nulled with a reason where deficit_svf == 0 — null, never 0, and never 100%.

key_light.label: winter solstice peak — the exact condition the recapture figure counts
key_light.frame: +x east, +y up, +z north; unit vector site -> sun
key_light.usage: to_sun_unit points FROM the site TO the sun. A Houdini distant light aims down its own -z, so orient it along light_travel_unit. Place the sun from this vector, never by eye — the caption has to be able to name the day.

stations.image: Stage 3 — Image A, the eye-level hero
stations.why_this_station: the worst enclosure on the line at which the canopy still demonstrably works AND the camera can stand in open air — 15.1% of winter sun recovered under a 6.83 m rib. Stations with a higher deficit exist; the ones that recover nothing are the section's subject rather than the hero's, and the ones whose camera falls inside a building are listed in `clearance.rejected_ahead_of_it`.

camera.framing: stands 25 m back along the deck and looks 40 m down it, so the hero rib sits in the middle distance with the canyon closing behind it

must_carry: real materiality on deck and steel
the towers in frame — the antagonist has to be visible

clearance.test_reason: a perspective plate has nothing cutting geometry away, so a buried target is a wall in frame
clearance.note: The unconstrained argmax is rank 0. Ranks skipped here were skipped because the camera could not be placed in open air, not because the selection rule changed.

svf_deck.gloss: sky view factor at the deck today (2.5-D isovist; reads systematically more open than Ladybug — never present raw and calibrated as interchangeable)

caveats_that_must_travel_with_it: Name the instrument. The independent Ladybug re-measure puts the field-driven enclosed-station mean at 17.39% against the hand-rolled 18.56% (data/envelope_validation.json).

Both recapture comparisons ARE significant at n = 159 and they point OPPOSITE ways: field-vs-(b) +1.18 pts [+0.26, +2.30] — the shaping beats the same steel spread flat — and field-vs-(a) -1.56 pts [-3.08, -0.03] — the uniform 7 m canopy recovers more, on 2.27x the steel. NEITHER SENTENCE MAY TRAVEL WITHOUT THE OTHER. The significance arrived with the sample (n 56 -> 159 after the re-fetch), not with a better design, and does not survive a 2005 pre-park baseline.
The recapture sensor is the rib apex, 1.20-7.23 m above the deck — sun reaching the structure, not sun reaching a person. Deck-level recapture is unmeasured.

nearest_wall_m.gloss: how much built context is actually within frame at this station

dom_occ_year.gloss: construction year of the dominant occluder — post-2009 means the enclosure in frame is tower-boom, not pre-existing fabric

stations.image: Stage 3b — Image B, the open contrast (river)
stations.selection_rule: max svf_deck subject to svf_deck >= 0.75 AND river_view (data/highline_viewshed.json) AND nearest_wall_m <= 40.0 (built context in frame)
stations.why_this_station: the deck open to its sky WITH the city still around it — the generator holds the rib near its minimum because svf_deck is already high, which is the design rule 'river-view segments aren't shaded' shown rather than asserted. The context gate is a hard constraint on the pool, not a post-hoc override; see `passed_over`.

camera.framing: along the deck, so the open sky above the flat rib is the subject
camera.aperture_note: aperture_az_deg 169.4 — swing toward this heading if the river itself must be in shot rather than the corridor.

passed_over.reason: This is the maximum-openness station on the line and it was PASSED OVER. Its nearest wall is 45.2 m away — the north rail-yard end, with effectively no built context in frame. An open contrast image has to show the deck open WITHIN the city; a station with no city in sight illustrates nothing about a corridor. It also has deficit_svf = 0.0, so its stored recapture of 1.000 is 100% of nothing and could not have been printed at all.
passed_over.not_a_data_problem: both facts are true properties of that station, correctly measured. It is the wrong station for this image, not a wrong number.

stations.alternates_rule: runners-up from the same context-gated pool, ordered by openness. Substituting one stays a sourced choice — re-run with the station changed rather than retyping numbers.

clearance.rule: max svf_deck subject to svf_deck >= 0.75, river_view, and nearest_wall_m <= 40.0
clearance.test_reason: a perspective plate has nothing cutting geometry away, so a buried target is a wall in frame

caption.title: IMAGE B · Stage 3b — the open contrast (river)
caption.caveats_trigger: include the caveats iff the plate prints recaptured_winter_sun_frac
caption.note: The subject of this plate is the FLAT rib over an open sky — the generator standing down where the deck can still see out. It is a plate about restraint, not about performance.

omitted_lines.status: OMITTED FROM THIS PLATE BY EDITORIAL CHOICE — the value is present and quotable in `numbers`, and is NOT suppressed.
omitted_lines.reason: This station's deficit_svf is ~0.01: it lost about one percent of its sky. The recapture fraction over that loss is real and passes the suppression rule, but on a plate a large-looking percentage sitting beside a near-zero deficit reads as the canopy performing, when what it actually describes is recovering a trivial loss. The number is not wrong; it is misleading at this station, and the honest fix is to leave it off rather than to print it with a disclaimer.
omitted_lines.not_a_threshold_change: The suppression rule is unchanged and stays `deficit_svf > 0 strictly`. Suppression is a property of the DATA (no loss means no recovery to measure); this omission is a property of THIS PLATE. Moving the threshold to catch this case would mean inventing a tuned cutoff, which is exactly what the project refuses to do elsewhere.
omitted_lines.if_you_want_it_back: add the line to B's caption template in pick_cameras.py and re-run; the value resolves from `numbers` and brings its three caveats with it.

stations.image: Stage 5b — Image C, the section through the worst core
stations.selection_rule: max deficit_svf over all 232 stations, subject to a camera position in open air
stations.why_this_station: the deepest core the tower boom created at which the section camera can stand in open air: 81.1% of the sky gone, a 7.03 m rib, and 0.0% winter sun recovered. The canopy at its most ambitious, failing — which THE_ANSWERING_LINE.md already states as the honest limit. Deeper cores exist; their cameras land inside the towers that make them deep, and they are listed in `clearance.rejected_ahead_of_it`.
stations.selection_trap_avoided: NOT selected on minimum svf_deck. s = 1004.7 m, s = 1503.1 m, s = 1511.1 m are the three lowest-svf_deck stations and every one of them has deficit_svf == 0.0 — always enclosed, nothing taken by the towers, ribs held at the generator minimum. A section drawn there would show enclosure this project does not claim to have measured the cause of.

camera.framing: true cross-section — 45 m perpendicular to the deck tangent, level at mid-rib height so the view is horizontal and the canyon walls stay parallel. Orthographic: a section that converges is a perspective, and the caption calls it a section.
camera.side_choice: the side the rib reaches away from, so the cantilever reads broadside rather than foreshortened

must_carry: the canyon walls at true height
a human figure on the deck for scale
the rib reaching and still not clearing the wall

clearance.test_reason: the section plane cuts everything nearer than the deck, and the worst core is inside a building because it IS the worst core
clearance.note: The unconstrained argmax is rank 0. Ranks skipped here were skipped because the camera could not be placed in open air, not because the selection rule changed.
